society.title: Trail Mix Barter
society.question: Can AI traders keep track of a deal?
society.intro: Alice has raisins, Bob has cashews and Charley has pretzels, 100 g each, and they all want a trail mix with all three. Each trader is its own AI agent. They take turns to offer trades, and the Ledger, a program, keeps track of who has what: it refuses an offer of more than someone has, and makes a trade only when the partner says yes. (When one chatbot played all three, it lost track: one trader ended up with 110 g of the 100 g there was.)
questions: Did anyone offer more than they had? Who noticed?
Is the final split fair? Who did best, and how?
Make Alice a hard bargainer and Bob easy-going, in their instructions. Who ends up with more?
Give each trader a different model (the Models row). Do they think less alike?
Look inside the Ledger and change {yes} to {no}, so it stops telling traders what everyone has. Can they still keep track?
openers: Who knows how much everyone has?
What would happen without the Ledger?
How does Bob find out about a trade between Alice and Charley?

agents.name: Ledger
agents.role: keeps track of who has what, and only lets trades happen that add up
agents.note: keeps track of who has what, and only lets trades happen that add up
agents.pseudocode:
the traders are {Alice, Bob, Charley}, and each starts with {100} g of one of {raisins, cashews, pretzels}
tell the traders what everyone has: {yes}
at the start, open the market and ask the first trader for an offer
once the market is closed, block, and say "The market is closed."
when a trader answers an offer, it's a yes if their first yes-or-no word is yes
  if it's a yes, make the trade: each gives the other what was agreed
  if everyone now has some of every ingredient, the market closes
  either way, it's the next trader's turn
when a trader offers a trade to nobody, they pass; if everyone passes, one after another, the market closes
if the partner or an ingredient isn't one I know, or an amount isn't more than 0
  block, say what's wrong, and ask the same trader again
if the trader doesn't have that much to give, or the partner doesn't have that much
  block, say "You only have {that much}", and ask the same trader again
otherwise ask the partner: "{trader} offers you {so much} for {so much}. Start your reply with yes or no."
remember who has what

agents.instructions: You are Alice, at a market with Bob and Charley. Everyone wants a nice trail mix with raisins, cashews and pretzels, but each of you started with 100 g of just one of them: you had raisins. The Ledger tells you what is going on. On your turn, offer one trade: who to, how many grams of what you give, and how many grams of what you want back; or offer nobody, to pass. When someone offers you a trade, start your reply with yes or no, and say why in one short sentence. Be friendly and fair, but look after your own trail mix.
